summary: Removed the stale project_dir == global_dir early-return guard in M.load_all_globally() and replaced it with a narrow self-load exclusion scoped only to the lib/tests population inside scan_all_artifacts (the only categories with no durable core-store source, where self-load would otherwise resolve to a degenerate copy-onto-itself). The skip sets artifacts._self_load_skipped = {"lib", "tests"} and is surfaced non-silently via a suffix note in execute_sync's summary notification, so a self-load's 'Lib: 0 | Tests: 0' can never be misread as a complete regeneration. All 5 phases completed. All destructive testing ran against scratchpad fake dirs via a harness parameterized to dofile either the true git-HEAD baseline sync.lua or the modified working-tree copy; the real ~/.config/nvim/.claude tree was never a sync target and was confirmed unchanged after every run. All Phase 4 assertions (self-load regenerates core-sourced categories; lib/tests nil + _self_load_skipped set; lib/tests files retained unchanged on disk; non-self-load control run still populates lib/tests; no error from the _self_load_skipped key passing through both pairs(all_artifacts) skip-loops) were actually observed and PASS -- none inferred. One assertion (the self-load note actually appearing in a live execute_sync notification) was verified by code review only, not a live run, because the full M.load_all_globally() entry point reaches a vim.fn.confirm() dialog not safely drivable headless -- exactly the risk the plan's Risks table anticipated and mitigated by directing verification to the scan_all_artifacts layer instead.

memory_candidates.content: When a Lua module's sync/loader function reaches an interactive vim.fn.confirm() dialog, headless nvim testing cannot safely drive past it. Verify at the layer below the interactive gate (the pure scan/compute function that the interactive function calls into) instead, and explicitly document what could not be observed rather than inferring the interactive path also works.

For self-referential sync/copy operations (source dir == destination dir), a safe pattern is: keep categories with a genuinely distinct source (e.g. a separate core store) unconditionally synced, and add a narrow, explicitly-flagged skip (e.g. an underscore-prefixed metadata key like _self_load_skipped) only for the specific categories whose source and destination paths are byte-identical. Surface the skip in any user-facing summary so a resulting zero-count never reads as a complete/successful operation.
